newsitem.title: EGYPT: Amnesty condemns Libya for flagrant rights abuses.
newsitem.headline: Amnesty condemns Libya for flagrant rights abuses.

text.p: Rights group Amnesty International criticised Libya on Tuesday for flagrant human rights violations, saying torture and extrajudicial killings of dissidents were rife in the North African state.

The group said in a faxed statement that disappearances, arbitrary arrests as well as blatant support by Libyan leader Muammar Gaddafi for the execution of opponents of his rule were an indication of a sinister human rights situation in Libya.

"In Libya, gross human rights violations are taking place not only with total impunity but they are also sanctioned at the highest level, in flagrant violation of the country's solemn obligations under human rights treaties," the statement said.
Libyan officials were not immediately available to comment.
In a report entitled "Libya: Gross human rights violations amid secrecy and isolation", Amnesty said that Gaddafi had made clear his disregard for human rights in recent speeches.
"I want a law to be introduced...so that the hands of the thief, both male and female, be cut off regardless of the amount they have stolen," Amnesty reported Gaddafi as saying.
"Anyone who has said 'no' would be seen as collaborating with the enemy. He (state official) has the right to shoot him dead often without trial or with a summary trial," Gaddafi said.
Amnesty said the Libyan General People's Congress had three months ago passed a law authorising collective punishment.
The law justifies Libyan officials taking entire families of suspected government opponents hostage and allows them to tear down the opponents' houses, the group said.

It also said human rights violations were common at detention centres and prisons. Amnesty said several prisoners had died as a result of torture, which includes electric shocks and being mauled by aggressive dogs.
Female detainees are also threatened with abuse, the group added.
Unlike several other countries which have taken promising steps towards improving their human rights record, Libya has increased the number of crimes punishable by death.

In July 1996, the General People's Committee for Justice and Public Security extended the death penalty to punish drug and alcohol-related crimes as well as people who speculate in food, clothes or housing during wars or blockades.
